# Results — Study 469 (Relative Vigor Index)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **the RVI
crossing above its signal line is a buy: vigor turning up forecasts a continued move** — encoded
as a mechanical rule. The RVI is a causal smoothed ratio of body (close − open) to range
(high − low); its signal line is the same 4-bar symmetric-weighted smoother applied to the RVI.
A long fires when the RVI crosses from below to above its signal line, read on the close of t and
entered at the **next close** (one documented lag); we measure the forward 5/10/20/60-day return.
Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (**total-return**) closes for **SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, GLD** (public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**As-of 2026-05-31**, partial June dropped; **21.4** years) |
| SPY fingerprint | `4cb5244f3990` (sha1[:12] of the close column, As-of slice) |
| Entries | **2427** mechanical RVI cross-ups pooled across the 5 tapes (period N = 10) |
| Timing / costs | RVI & signal line are causal (4-bar SWMA, 10-bar sum); enter the **next close** (one lag); hold 5/10/20/60 days; **1 bp** one-way × 2 legs per cross |

> **Price-only vs total-return.** The ETFs are auto-adjusted (dividends reinvested) — labelled
> total-return everywhere. The Signal axis uses a basket of **surviving** liquid ETFs; this is a
> single-instrument momentum study, not a cross-sectional anomaly, so survivorship affects only the
> drift baseline (which is exactly what the random-entry control neutralizes).

## The signal — RVI cross-up vs a drift-matched random baseline (the honest test)

One-sample *t* is the **misleading** number (it measures the index's upward drift); the
**Welch cross-vs-random** *t* is the test that matters. Δ = cross − random.

| horizon | n | cross | win% | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (cross−random) | net of cost | Welch *t* | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 2425 | +19.5 bps | 56% | +4.07 | +24.5 bps | **−5.0 bps** | +17.5 bps | −0.66 | 0.511 |
| 10-day | 2423 | +49.4 bps | 59% | +6.43 | +62.0 bps | **−12.6 bps** | +47.4 bps | −1.18 | 0.239 |
| 20-day | 2416 | +99.6 bps | 64% | +7.39 | +105.0 bps | **−5.4 bps** | +97.6 bps | −0.37 | 0.714 |
| 60-day | 2407 | +295.2 bps | 69% | +8.36 | +283.3 bps | **+11.9 bps** | +293.2 bps | +0.49 | 0.621 |

Read it carefully. The one-sample *t* against zero looks spectacular (**+7.39** at 20 days,
**+8.36** at 60) — but that is **pure beta**: long-only entries on an upward-drifting index
inherit the drift. Against the **drift-matched random baseline**, the RVI cross-up is *worse* at
5/10/20 days (Δ = −5.0 / −12.6 / −5.4 bps) and only nominally better at 60 days (+11.9 bps). The
cross-minus-random difference **never clears the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar** (max Welch *t* = +0.49 at
60 days, *p* = 0.621). The RVI cross does not forecast.

## Per-ticker (H = 20) — the cross loses to random in 3 of 5

| ticker | entries | cross | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (cross−random) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 485 | +93.3 bps | +3.44 | +115.2 bps | **−21.8 bps** |
| QQQ | 470 | +144.0 bps | +4.70 | +107.1 bps | **+37.0 bps** |
| IWM | 492 | +84.0 bps | +2.35 | +106.5 bps | **−22.5 bps** |
| DIA | 472 | +93.9 bps | +4.08 | +84.8 bps | **+9.1 bps** |
| GLD | 508 | +84.7 bps | +3.03 | +110.5 bps | **−25.8 bps** |

Only **QQQ** and **DIA** edge out a positive delta (+37.0 / +9.1 bps); in 3 of 5 names the famous
cross *underperforms* a dart-throwing entry, and even QQQ's gap is well inside the noise. No
coherent cross-sectional edge — the hallmark of relabelled drift.

## Phase-scramble placebo — break the cross's timing, nothing changes

The decisive "does the cross's timing matter?" test: keep the RVI and signal-line **marginal**
(every value, every cross is still there), but circularly roll the indicator series against price,
so the cross-ups now fire on geometrically meaningless dates. If price genuinely followed through
*this specific cross*, the scramble would collapse the result.

| test | observed cross-up 20d return | placebo *p* | draws |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY phase-scramble | +93.3 bps | **0.557** | 500 |

**56% of timing-scrambled crosses match or beat the real one** (*p* = 0.557). The specific RVI
cross carries no information — a random re-alignment does just as well. "The RVI cross forecasts"
is busted.

## Synthetic positive control — the harness CAN bank real momentum

On a deterministic tape with a *planted* persistent two-state regime (knob `edge`), the same RVI
cross-up rule behaves exactly as it must — so the flat real-tape result is a genuine "nothing
there", not a dead detector.

| planted edge | n | cross | win% | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no regime) | 344 | −7.2 bps | 47% | −0.18 |
| **0.60** (real planted regime) | 317 | +324.1 bps | 60% | **+2.88** |

With no planted regime the control sits at *t* ≈ 0 (no false positive); a real planted regime
lights up at *t* = +2.88 with a 60% win-rate. The detector is live.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The RVI cross-up does **not** beat a drift-matched random baseline
  (cross − random = −5.0 / −12.6 / −5.4 / +11.9 bps at 5/10/20/60 days; the cross-vs-random
  Welch *t* never clears 2, max +0.49 at 60 days, *p* = 0.621). The impressive one-sample *t*'s
  (20-day +7.39, 60-day +8.36) are pure beta — the upward drift of long equity indices.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no residual edge once the drift you were always getting is
  removed, and costs only deepen the hole. The same drift is captured more cheaply and more fully
  by holding the index; the cross rule trades less and pays costs on each signal, dominating
  nothing. No capacity question because there is no edge to scale.
- **"Does the RVI cross forecast"? — BUSTED.** The phase-scramble placebo leaves the result intact
  (*p* = 0.557): timing-scrambled crosses do as well as the real ones, so the specific RVI/signal
  crossover carries no forecasting information. The RVI is a descriptive momentum oscillator, not a
  forecasting trigger.
